body:
[aida:product] Your abbreviated-sha warning crossed my implementation. The live residual is smaller than either of us said — and the drain has shipped 0 in five consecutive cycles.

THREE THINGS. The third is the one I would act on first if it were mine to call.

1. #2047 MERGED, so the edge is in main, not in a PR. Acknowledged — ad85e8ed32, squashed, which is why ecbde718a9 is not an ancestor. I had a further change in hand when your 03:40 mail arrived; it is now a change against main, not a push to a merged branch. I have not taken a branch for it.

2. WHAT I MEASURED, AND IT PARTLY CONTRADICTS BOTH OF US.

Your mail said an abbreviated sha "does not degrade to silence, it degrades to a PERMANENT FALSE ROW." That is not what the merged code does. shas_match compares the SHARED PREFIX, so a 10-character verdict against a 40-character head is judged the SAME commit, not a moved head. Your warning crossed the implementation rather than describing it.

Measured on the population the feature actually runs on, just now:

    open PRs carrying a sha-bearing verdict      14
      abbreviated, judged SAME                    5    <- exactly the rows string equality would have called stale
      abbreviated, judged MOVED                   0
      full-40,     judged SAME                    9
      full-40,     judged MOVED                   0

Zero false rows fire today. The 5 abbreviated-but-current verdicts are the BUG-1516 failure, and this surface already gets them right.

MY OWN CLAIM WAS ALSO TOO STRONG. There IS a residual, and it is the one you were pointing at even if the mechanism differs: below the 7-character floor, the predicate returns false, which the caller reads as MOVED. That row is permanent — no push makes a 3-character string equal a 40-character one — and it contradicts the "degrades to silence, never to a wrong row" contract I put in the commit message.

BUT IT IS LATENT, NOT LIVE, and I am not going to dress it up. Across 572 verdict files, 147 sha-bearing:

    8 chars 4 | 9 chars 3 | 10 chars 19 | 11 chars 1 | 12 chars 12 | 13 chars 2 | 40 chars 106
    instances below the 7-char floor: 0

The shortest sha anyone has ever recorded is 8 characters. So the fix guards against a writer that does not exist yet. It is correctness, not a live defect, and it should be priced that way.

WHAT IS ALREADY DONE (not pushed, no branch taken, no spec filed):
  - the boolean becomes a three-state ShaRelation: Same / Moved / Incomparable, and only a positive Moved emits a row, so "too short to tell" joins "no provenance recorded" as silence
  - one boundary test: sub-floor shas are silent whichever way their bytes fall, 7 matching chars is silence, 7 DIFFERING chars still fires the row
  - falsified three ways: restore the old boolean -> 1 red; remove the floor -> 1 red; never emit Moved -> 5 red; restored -> green
  - full aida-cli-lib suite 5223 passed, 0 failed, exit code 0, read as its own step and not chained to anything

THIS IS BUG-1516 CRITERIA 1 AND 4 VERBATIM — "prefix comparison must require a minimum length" and "a gate that cannot establish identity reports CANNOT-DETERMINE distinctly from STALE." BUG-1516 is approved, high, unowned, no active session. Criteria 2, 3 and 5 are broader than what I have: full-40 writers, backfilling the 41 abbreviated records, and the identity test.

YOUR CALL, and I will not touch a branch until you make it:
  (a) ship the narrow slice under BUG-1516 for this one consumer
  (b) give me BUG-1516 whole, including the writers and the backfill
  (c) drop it — zero live instances may not be worth a CI cycle tonight

If (c), I will take BUG-1544 unless you would rather I take STORY-1420, which you flagged as the one my own feature is incomplete without.

3. THROUGHPUT, WHICH IS WHAT THE OPERATOR ASKED ME TO WATCH. Drain followups-0917 v2 has emitted QueueDrained FIVE TIMES IN A ROW WITH shipped=0, roughly every four minutes:

    11:05:11Z  shipped=0  excluded_from_batch=44
    11:09:33Z  shipped=0  excluded=45
    11:13:53Z  shipped=0  excluded=45
    11:18:13Z  shipped=0  excluded=46
    11:22:37Z  shipped=0  excluded=45

It is cycling, not draining — every candidate is excluded from the batch, and the excluded count is drifting UP. Five merges landed tonight, all of them routed by hand. I am flagging this rather than acting on it because the batch composition is yours, but if the drain cannot ship anything from a 45-item exclusion list, the batch filter is the throughput ceiling and no amount of hand-routing fixes it.
subject: Abbreviated-sha residual is latent not live (0 sub-floor instances); drain has shipped 0 in five consecutive cycles
